Solution written to `/home/kara/SOLUTION.md`. Here's a summary of what I found and verified:

## Diagnosis (reproduced exactly)

Installed node-duckdb 1.4.4, pointed `HOME` at an empty dir (cold `~/.duckdb/extensions`, emulating a fresh runner), and ran the pre-fix code `LOAD fts;`:

```
IO Error: Extension ".../v1.4.4/linux_amd64/fts.duckdb_extension" not found.
Extension "fts" is an existing extension.  Install it first using "INSTALL fts".
```

Identical to the CI failure. Root cause: FTS bootstrap only did `LOAD fts` (relying on auto-install, which fails on ephemeral runners), unlike the repo's VSS bootstrap which already does `INSTALL vss` + `LOAD vss`.

## Two non-obvious findings that shape the fix

1. **`INSTALL fts` is idempotent** — re-running it after a successful install is a verified no-op, so calling it unconditionally is safe.
2. **node-duckdb 1.4.4's `db.exec(sql)` without a callback silently swallows errors** — no Promise, no throw (verified: `await db.exec('BAD SQL')` prints "no error thrown", exit 0). So the documented fix must use a promisify wrapper or callbacks — a bare `try/await/catch` would not catch anything. Likewise, the CI pre-install snippet from the problem description fails silently offline (exit 0), so I provide a fail-loud callback version.

## Verified end-to-end (all scenarios passed)

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Cold runner, pre-fix `LOAD fts` only | FAIL — exact CI error |
| Cold runner, `INSTALL fts` → `LOAD fts` | PASS, extension cached |
| Cold runner + offline (bogus repo, no cache) | Clear error naming `"fts"` + INSTALL detail + network guidance |
| Warm cached runner + fully offline, `LOAD` only | PASS (proves actions/cache works) |
| Re-`INSTALL fts` on cached env | No-op, PASS |

The markdown contains the complete solution: the `ensureFtsExtension` helper (`src/duckdb/fts.ts`), the bootstrap call-site change, the CI YAML (actions/cache on `~/.duckdb/extensions` keyed by `runner.os`/`runner.arch`/duckdb version + the fail-loud pre-install step), a full verification section with every command and observed output, and a note that the GAP-012-style empty test counts are a symptom, not the bug (test count kept identical).

signatures.description: Symptom: CI (GitHub Actions, node-duckdb 1.4.4) fails 10 vitest tests in a DuckDB FTS search suite with `IO Error: Extension "/home/runner/.duckdb/extensions/v1.4.4/linux_amd64/fts.duckdb_extension" not found. Extension "fts" is an existing extension. Install it first using "INSTALL fts".` Downstream: `SearchIndexMissingError: No keyword search index for namespace .../.search`. Locally the suite is green because ~/.duckdb/extensions already has the extension cached — the bug only appears on cold environments. Root cause: code did only `LOAD fts;` (relying on DuckDB auto-install, which fails on fresh runners); the repo's own VSS code (src/duckdb/vss.ts) uses the correct pattern: explicit `INSTALL vss` then `LOAD vss` in try/catch. Fix (proven locally against a cold extension_directory): (1) before LOAD, run explicit idempotent `INSTALL fts;` — INSTALL on an already-installed extension is a no-op; on INSTALL error still attempt LOAD, throw clear error naming the extension + network requirement if both fail; (2) in CI workflow add a pre-install step (`node -e "const {Database}=require('duckdb'); const db=new Database(':memory:'); db.exec('INSTALL fts'); db.exec('LOAD fts'); db.close();"`) plus actions/cache on ~/.duckdb/extensions. Note: GAP-012-style 'assert docs test counts' steps print empty counts when the vitest summary contains failures — that is a symptom, not the bug. Kept test count identical (no new tests).
